body: Ha, I've been dutifully forwarding these arguments along to all my dependencies all this time without realizing they inherit the caller's options.

Thanks again for the PR!

See also [comment](https://lobste.rs/c/fh1njp) from @andrewrk, copied here in case the lobsters thread disappears:

> The C preprocessor is a safer dependency than a linker feature. Linker functionality is not standardized and different features have different degrees of how prevalent they are among the linker implementations. Linker arguments also bypass the compiler frontend and can therefore cause confusing problems that the compiler can't help troubleshoot because it doesn't understand semantically what your linker arguments are doing. In general it's better to avoid passing arguments to the linker.
>
> With Zig specifically, all linker arguments are implemented in the frontend, understood by the compiler, and filtered down to the linker layer. This means however that arbitrary linker arguments are not supported; only those which have been properly integrated with the compiler. You can't just bypass the compiler and give args to the linker.
>
> For this particular -wrap feature, however, it looks like zig does have support for it. Looks like it hasn't been integrated with the -fno-lld linkers yet though.

(Whoops, sorry for letting this sit--I had notifications off by mistake.)

I think this is a great idea. I'm not a fan of the C API, and regardless, it's nice to have integration with Zig's error handling and such.

The right way to do this IMO is to keep this repo unopinionated--have it continue to just expose the C API as is--but then have a separate repo imports this one, and wraps it with the Zig bindings. (This is also the approach suggested by [AYC](https://github.com/allyourcodebase/#im-a-zig-user-and-i-want-to-contribute-a-repository-how-can-i-do-it)).

If you're still interested in this project and are down to split it into a separate repo, I can add a link from the README to point people to it!
(btw thanks for the updates for latest Zig!)

Nice work, thanks for the PR!

I'm going to dig into this more tomorrow, these are some notes mostly for myself:
* [x] Caching `c.zig` may no longer be necessary if the necessary translate C fixes landed in Zig 0.16 #6
* [ ] This PR resolves #5
* [ ] This PR resolves #3
* [x] It looks like `stat` was removed from std [here](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/commit/6216922a9d63982f11ff8ee551a6688bc873e51c) because its layout isn't well defined. As a result, we should probably grab this struct from the libc header directly rather than defining it ourselves
* [x] I have some minor changes I need to clean up and push
* [ ] I'll check on whether Zin is being updated for 0.16, or look into demoing video play another way

Nice! I'll check over this tomorrow. I reached out to Johnny offline about zin, I'll likely reimplement the video play example in zigx which will make the upgrade easier.

That's too bad about translate C still failing to translate the pipewire headers. I'll look into the error--now that it's able to be called via the build system there are some more options to play with. If there's not away around it I'll file an issue on the translate C project, we won't have to wait for the next language release to update translate C anymore.

Just checked out the stat changes--looks good to me. I'm working on porting the video play example, and seeing if I can get rid of c.zig using the translate C package, or alternatively, file any issues I run into upstream.

This is pending on two upstream issues being resolved:
* [ ] [Translate C failing to pull in libc on nixos](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/translate-c/issues/317#issuecomment-13237302)
* [ ] [Issue with some Pipewire static asserts](https://codeberg.org/ziglang/translate-c/issues/322)
    * I've worked around this one locally, so it's not technically blocking
    * [This open PR](https://github.com/Vexu/arocc/pull/995) resolves the issue

~~In the mean time, I'm going to set up translate C support behind a flag, to make repros and migrating away from the cached c.zig file easier.~~

I've decided to remove `c.zig` despite this issues, since you can work around it by adding `libc` to your nix flakes. I don't think this should be necessary, but it's easier to use the workaround for now than to maintain the cached results in `c.zig`.

I'll rename this issue and keep it open until no workaround are necessary.

I just pushed some changes to this branch that add a `-Duse_translate_c` option. We can't yet make this default (see #6) but it should work on non nixOS machines, I have a workaround for the error you hit in place. Once the issue on nixOS is resolved upstream I'll drop the cached translations, that doesn't have to block this PR though.

I'll wrap up porting the video play example soon and push it here, then we should be ready to merge. In the mean time this branch should be usable for Awebo dev on 0.16 regardless of the example working--if there's anything blocking you let me know!
